desc: Understand problem: pair N cakes into K pairs to maximize sum of max(X_a+X_b, Y_a+Y_b, Z_a+Z_b)
Recognize that dominant group heuristic fails on counterexamples
Implement binary search on C in [0, 2*10^9]
For each C, filter cakes with x,y,z <= C
Use sweep + Fenwick tree to find max matching in O(N log N) per check
Handle K pairs requirement, return True if matching of size K exists
Verify edge cases (N=2, K=1; all zeros; large N)
Ensure sum of N over T is at most 1e5, so O(T * N log^2 N) fits

Implement the `feasible(C)` function using a sweep on X-sorted cakes and a segment tree or Fenwick tree of sorted Z-values indexed by Y to efficiently find a partner satisfying all three sum constraints.
Add binary search on C from 0 to 2*10^9 (or the maximum possible sum) to find the maximum C where `feasible(C)` is true.
